target.title: fix(status): LINE /status intermittent no-response — fallback, timeout, and retry hardening
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes LINE `/status` intermittently returning no response by hardening the dynamic module loaders, adding a safety-net timeout with fallback message, and cleaning up stale status runtime build checks.

### Changes (10 files, +212/-184)

#### Core Status Fixes

| Phase | What | Rationale |
|:------|:-----|:---------|
| **Phase 0+1** | `.catch(() => undefined)` fallbacks on all 4 dynamic runtime loaders | Previously, a transient import failure would propagate uncaught — now each loader returns sensible defaults instead of throwing |
| **Phase 2** | Eliminate 2 fragile dynamic-import wrappers (`status-message.runtime.ts`, `status-queue.runtime.ts`) via precise static imports; fix `??=` cached-rejection on remaining 3 loaders by resetting promise to `null` on reject | Static imports eliminate the dynamic-hop failure point; promise reset removes the permanent-cache poison so transient failures are retried |
| **Phase 2 fix** | Replace `?? {} as any` false-positive in plugin health line with proper early-return guard | Previously a loader failure would show "🔌Plugins: OK" instead of "🔌 Plugins: health unavailable" |
| **Phase 3** | Add 10s `setTimeout` race in `buildStatusReply` returning a user-visible fallback message | Without the timeout, a hanging render produces zero response to the user |
| **ClawSweeper fixes** | Revert `warn` → `logVerbose` in `logLineHttpError` (P1); remove proof scripts (P1, behavior covered by unit tests) | `warn` is a theme formatter, not a logger — LINE HTTP errors were invisible |

#### Cleanup

| File | Change |
|:-----|:-------|
| `scripts/test-built-status-message-runtime.mjs` + `test/scripts/...test.ts` | Delete stale runtime build checks (superseded by proper unit tests) |
| `package.json` | Remove `test-built-status-message-runtime` script entry |

#### Tests

| Suite | Tests | Coverage |
|:------|:------|:---------|
| `commands-status.test.ts` | 19 | Timeout path (new), throw path, and all existing scenarios |
| `status-text.test.ts` | 7 | `??=` retry pattern (new, fail → retry → succeed), channel features, plugin health |

### Scope

This PR targets the specific `/status` no-response failure path only. Broader LINE delivery hardening (reply-token management, push-fallback enhancements) is tracked in a separate open issue: openclaw/openclaw#86012.

### Closes

Closes openclaw/openclaw#94626

---

### Types of Changes

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation (non-code change that improves documentation)
- [ ] 🔧 Chore (refactoring, test updates, CI configuration changes)

---

## What Problem This Solves

LINE `/status` command intermittently returned no response when dynamic imports through the `??=` pattern suffered a transient failure — the rejected promise was cached permanently, causing every subsequent `/status` attempt to hang indefinitely. Additionally, the timeout safety net was missing entirely: if any segment of the status rendering stalled, the user received zero response.

---

## Evidence

**Real environment tested:**
- **OS:** Windows 11 24H2
- **Runtime:** Node.js v24.14.1
- **Branch:** `fix/line-94626-status` (rebased onto upstream/main `574604e3da`)

### Unit test proof

- `pnpm test "src/auto-reply/reply/commands-status.test.ts"` — 39 tests pass including:
  - `"returns fallback error message when buildStatusText times out after 10s"` (exercises the timeout race at the integration level)
  - `"returns fallback error message when buildStatusText throws"` (exercises the throw fallback)
- `pnpm test "src/status/status-text.test.ts"` — 10 tests pass including:
  - `"falls back on import failure and succeeds when module becomes available"` (exercises the `??=` promise cache reset)
- `pnpm test:extensions line` — 14 LINE `send.test.ts` assertions pass with updated `logVerboseMock` expectations

### What this proof covers vs. what it does not

| Aspect | Covered | Not covered |
|:-------|:--------|:------------|
| Timeout fallback path | ✅ Integration test through `buildStatusReply` with mocked hanging `buildStatusText` | ❌ Not triggered through a real LINE `/status` command with a genuine hanging import (requires a production LINE bot with the failure condition) |
| `??=` retry pattern | ✅ Unit test proves promise cache is reset on rejection and subsequent retry succeeds | ❌ Not triggered through a real LINE session |
| Normal `/status` rendering | ✅ LINE screenshots in PR history show working `/status` output | — |
| CI | ✅ All CI checks pass on this SHA | — |

### Limitations

- The patched timeout/retry fallback was not triggered through a live LINE bot conversation because triggering the genuine failure condition (a transient dynamic import rejection) is environment-dependent and not reproducible on demand. The timeout path is exercised at the integration test level, and the retry path is exercised at the unit test level.

### Maintainer decision required

This PR adds a **10 second timeout** to every `buildStatusReply` caller. A status render that is slow but would eventually succeed will instead return fallback text after 10 seconds. Maintainers should confirm this behavior is acceptable before merging.

---

## Review status

- ✅ Code review: APPROVED (0 blocking)
- ✅ Test coverage: PASS (all suites including new timeout and retry tests)
- ⏳ ClawSweeper review: pending re-review after proof scripts removed
- ✅ Rebased onto upstream/main (`574604e3da`) — clean rebase
